samples.summary: No test asserts merge propagation is persisted to the store; all assertions read the in-memory map
samples.evidence: Every new test asserts via `sheet.getMerges()` (merge.test.ts:107, 137, 182, 206, 225), which is the sync accessor returning `this.merges` directly (sheet.ts:763-765). The new code additionally calls `await this.store.deleteMerge(...)` and `await this.store.setMerge(...)` (sheet.ts:2366, 2375) — the persistence half of the change. If both store calls were deleted, all six tests would still pass, yet the merge would be lost on reload/collaboration. `Store.getMerges()` is available and async (memory.ts:467) and `Sheet.load` reads from it (sheet.ts:497), so a `await store.getMerges()` assertion is easy and absent.
searchedFor: grep getMerges|setMerge|deleteMerge in packages/sheets/test (only sheet.getMerges() hits in merge.test.ts)

samples.summary: Style-preserving branch of the destination-clearing loop is untested
samples.evidence: sheet.ts:2387-2391 branches: a destination cell hidden under the moved merge keeps its style (`store.set(ref, { s: cell.s })`) but loses content, otherwise it is deleted. The only test of this loop ('should clear destination cells covered by the moved merge', merge.test.ts:143-164) writes a plain value 'ghost' with no style, so only the `delete` branch runs. Nothing checks that a styled covered cell keeps its style.

samples.summary: The movedAnchors exclusion for overlapping source/destination has no test
samples.evidence: sheet.ts:2297-2303 filters source merges out of `overwrittenMerges` specifically because source and destination can overlap; without that filter an overlapping drag of a merged block would be wrongly rejected (its merge range is not fully inside destRange). All new tests move from row 1 to row 3 with non-overlapping ranges (merge.test.ts:99-105, 129-135, 152-158, 174-180, 198-204, 217-223), so this guard is never exercised — a regression removing the filter would keep the suite green.
searchedFor: read all six new tests' moveRangeTo arguments

samples.summary: The ordering claim (merge update must precede recalculation) is untested
samples.evidence: The comment at sheet.ts:2360-2363 states the merge pass must run before the recalculation because `expandChangedSrefsWithMergeAliases` (sheet.ts:2403) needs the new layout. No new test contains a formula at all — no cell referencing a covered destination cell (e.g. `=B3+1` after a merge lands on A3:C3) — so moving the merge block after the recalculation would not fail any test.

samples.summary: Trivially-true assertion in the no-merge test
samples.evidence: `expect(sheet.getMerges().size).toBe(0)` in 'should move plain cells when no merge is involved' holds regardless of the change — the test never creates a merge, and no code path in `moveRangeTo` can create one from nothing (`movedMerges` is empty). The remaining two assertions in the test are meaningful, so this is cosmetic.

All six tests use one 1xN merge (rs: 1). Neither a multi-row merge span (which exercises the row loop in `mergeCoveredSrefs`) nor a source range containing two merges (the `for (const merge of movedMerges)` loop with more than one element, sheet.ts:2369) is covered.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. All six drag-move tests assert only via sheet.getMerges() (merge.test.ts:107,137,182,206,225), which returns the in-memory map directly (sheet.ts:763-765). The new propagation pass writes to the store separately (sheet.ts:2366, 2375), and MemStore holds an independent map (memory.ts:459-469, getMerges returns a copy); tests construct `new Sheet(new MemStore())` and never call loadMerges, so removing both store calls would leave every assertion green — the persistence half is untestable-by-these-tests. Wide counterexample search found none: repo-wide greps for getMerges/setMerge/deleteMerge hit only merge.test.ts among tests; loadMerges appears in tests only in concurrency-driver.ts:18 (setup, and that suite never calls moveRangeTo); moveRangeTo appears only in sheet.ts, view/worksheet.ts, merge.test.ts and task docs, so no view/frontend/concurrency/harness test reaches the changed path. In-memory propagation IS meaningfully covered (not vacuous), but the persisted half of the new behavior has no test at all, which is the "missing tests" lane; a store.getMerges() round-trip assertion is readily available (memory.ts:467, sheet.ts:496-497).
